parsed.explanation: No traveler-facing exposure is documented: no offence of trans presentation, no facility/birth-sex rule, no border document friction, no police targeting, no trans-specific violence. Structural signals are positive — functioning courts and parliament (marriage equality, partnerships), an anti-discrimination code, active equality organisations, and a tourism product built on LGBT welcome. Against that, protections are written for sexual orientation only, so a trans visitor's formal recourse is thin; acceptance is documented as conditional ('not in their face'), religious influence is the named brake, and government itself opposed equality in the 2004-07 litigation. Trans-specific data (custody, wards, border practice) is absent, so those remain open questions, not exposures. Recent harassment is undocumented but the record itself warns silence proves nothing. Net: reduced risk with genuine acceptance but no trans-specific legal shield.
